findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached FLOWR endpoint VJP, so coordinate contrasts are not physical interaction energies.

The observed window is the score-clock interval [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score times, and the curve support is [0.0, 0.49]; recorded affinities are removed and an equal score prior is used, so no decoded terminal affinity labels are available for this study.

Continuous contrast features over the observed support are non-monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass shows 4 sign changes with first_rate_z positive and last_rate_z negative, and landmark_00_local_dx shows 6 sign changes with strong sign conflicts, so a constant rule is not supported and any time-conditioned rule must stay within observed-node interpolation.

Several local coordinate contrasts have large-magnitude rate z-scores at the window edges (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z strongly negative, last_rate_z positive) with relative node RMSE well above zero and polynomial_accepted false, indicating rate changes that are not well described by an accepted polynomial fit.
landmark_00_local_dz shows 10 sign changes and 7 strong sign conflicts with whole_window_z near zero, so its whole-window mean is not a reliable signed direction despite large first_rate_z.

hypotheses.falsifier: No improvement in observed-node fit fidelity versus a constant-sign rule, or sign pattern not reproducible across independent batches.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass contrast sign and rate over observed score times
hypotheses.scope: observed window [0.0, 0.5], predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast rule that follows the observed-node sign of landmark_00_soft_mass (positive early, negative late) will track the observed contrast better than a constant-sign rule over [0.0, 0.5].

hypotheses.direction: rate-change diagnostic, not a velocity target
hypotheses.falsifier: A constant-rate fit accepted with low relative node RMSE and consistent sign across batches.
hypotheses.observable: first_rate_z versus last_rate_z sign reversal for landmark_00_local_dy
hypotheses.scope: observed window, predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: The large edge rate z-scores in landmark_00_local_dy reflect within-window rate changes rather than a stable cohort-level shift, and would not persist under a constant rule.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Only continuous_trends rows were read; branch_adjusted, survival_effects, increment_effects, turnover_accounting, joint_diagnostics and regional_effects were not inspected, so multiplicity-adjusted support, joint coupling and turnover accounting remain unassessed.
Contrast curves are coordinate contrasts, not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies.
No current study outcome data are available to this role.
